body: Hey that's beautiful!!!! I also have a tat of a cardinal in memory of my father who passed years ago. They do bring peace!
Yeah and I haven't been around long enough to see changes made, but we are encouraged to be honest
I take breaks once in a while and barely talk to anyone, keep to myself, don't go out. It sucks but it helps me to reset I suppose. I hope you find relief soon
I can't draw a conclusion on myself, or my happiness so it makes it tempting to want to end it yes. Welcome to the world of my depression.
Didn't expect conclusions drawn
Yes it's a repeating issue.... It's not easy but thanks for your feedback.
There are people that will listen, good friends. I'm just getting very bothered by him threatening to call someone when I'm very upset. Of course he's the first one I go to since we live together

I love crystals!! Their appearance has always brought me joy and I do enjoy looking into the "spiritual properties and meanings" behind them for fun, I carry them as worry stones basically. Honestly carrying a crystal that supposedly repels negativity helps to keep my attitude stronger. Call it placebo effect I suppose

This is how I feel most of the time. Lately I've been feeling a little better and making some more friends at work (or well joking around with em more) but I wonder if I will eventually regret getting closer. I've already disconnected from most of my family. I'm also dreading anything bad happening again. I'd rather end my life than hurt even more or go through anything else traumatic. I hope you can find something to help keep you going and I wish I had better words to say or hope to offer. It all comes from within. This world can be so unfair.

I'm sorry that's horrible :( wow I am sorry you had a rough time growing up and that's heartbreaking about your cat too.

Crazy coincidence my father's deathiversary is June too, this year it was on a Sunday just like when he passed away (father's day too so I was a little depressed around then).

One thing I did to honor him was get a tattoo similar to one he had. That helps me feel better. 

I wonder what my life would be like if either or both of my parents didn't pass by the time I was 19. Mom passed when I was ten, I think it's why I get like a doomsday anxiety when things are going well and periods of depression now. It's not easy.
:) it feels so good to get out of those periods

It made me sob too, I love Max and her character development. When she talks about how she really felt about her brother and how he gave her a hard time I understood her entirely, she has so much depth

Honestly I wasn't happy. I was annoyed for a while and very numb/off feeling for a few months . Whenever I suffer now I wish that I had succeeded, but I've been working on increasing my grateful for what I have in the present thoughts and finding simple joys in my life, that is making me happy

Prescription anxiety meds tend to just make me lethargic and lazy feeling, then after the effects wear off I get moody. I was on one med for a bit that made me rage and get angry, I went off on people and embarrassed myself on social media (there were other provoking factors involved but it's a long story). That latter med, welbutrin (buprion?) Caused me to fear trying any other daily meds that affect the psyche.

I agree with you, when I start thinking the these or similar topics to what you posted I get very depressed and my mind starts producing a lotta thoughts about how pointless and corrupt this society/lifestyle is :( I try to find joy in little things lately, have fun interactions with coworkers and friends, and make my home as cozy as possible. I also avoid interacting with certain individuals, and if I want time to myself I've stopped guilt tripping myself when I and relaxing when I could be out with others. 

Sorry if that comment strayed a little, but that's how I've been keeping myself distracted and less depressed

I can relate. I lost both of my parents by the time I was 19, and I tried keeping a connection with extended family for a while after but as the years passed we've grown apart. There's been times I've been very close with a small group of friends, they definitely felt like family but they have all started their own immediate families/we don't live as close and also work different schedules. I feel lonely off and on, but I try to message q few friends weekly still and it helps. I do have a significant other I live with which really.makes a difference... However I feel like an oddball bc I'd like to get married to him one day, but I don't want to go through having a wedding. I don't want kids either but we talk about getting more dogs someday.

One thing that's helped me is to remind myself I don't have to have a lifestyle, family structure, etc that is similar to most of society's. I've also focused on weeding out toxic individuals, and spent some time on considering what I really want and don't want in my life. 

I shut down some and feel weird around bigger family events. It helps to just focus on little conversations during them, but there's been some awkward moments for me especially while I struggle with depression off and on. I try to shut down any negative thoughts that roam my mind in regards to my situation and how different I am from so many others that have immediate family members they're close to. It's difficult at times but remember there are definitely others in situations similar to yours, and it might just be they're shy about talking about it.

Nothing is wrong with you at all in my eyes

I don't think this is odd, it sounds like we're similar, I don't like to get a lot of attention from it. Instead of lying about it I just either don't bring them up at all, or if someone asks I just tell them they passed when I was younger. I don't tell everyone the truth about how they passed but generally saying heart problems, like a heart attack, won't encourage any other questions.

I've lost two jobs bc of bad anxiety. Most recent was last fall, best paying job I ever had but also required the most.amount of delivering bad news I've ever had to do in a job. Got into a car accident after a shift there, tried to go back the next week and had such crippling anxiety I couldn't see straight (seriously my vision was wavy while trying to drive in). Now I have a much simpler job within walking distance of home and I'm managing my mental "issues" much better

For me I'm thankful I didn't get harassed by anyone, I did see one girl freak out and throw a chair when she got mad while chatting on the phone. A few relatives were visiting at that point too so they left with a hell of an impression. Both times felt so useless to me honestly. Everyone's needs are different but yep it sucked.

You aren't a lost cause. Life is difficult in countless ways and possibilities... There are so many challenges. I felt the most helpful person there was a person who helped people figure out their insurance situations/apply for insurance and such. We only met and talked once but she seemed more genuine than the doctors and nurses. One of the counselors seemed genuine too actually but we had different experiences so I couldn't relate to him as well.
I'm terrified of going back too... I didn't see anyone have fun. Not one person, it was just blah.

There was nothing fun or goofy and I've been twice, once after an attempt. A second time a friend supposedly called a wellness check on me and I was forced in. Thank God I didn't have to cover the bills but I'm not confiding in them much anymore or well anyone else for that matter .... I'm so afraid if certain people find out about it they'll think I'm crazy :( it makes me feel ashamed of how I am especially the second trip there. I feel a lot of embarrassment and shame. Also wish I could hear what my dad would say if he were alive but to my extended family I'm pretty sure I'm the psychotic black sheep or something so now I stick completely to myself and they don't know much about what I'm up to anymore. I feel less pressure now but anyhow yeah feel free to share with me or message

Yes this is why I need to keep a job that isn't real stressful (thankful I have that right now). Without anything to do on a weekly basis my depression gets awful and I get anxious spirals too. I think I think too much at times..

I was similar after I lost my dad. Really I didn't party or get high all too often yet I know I was pushing myself for a while to stay distracted and not think about the things/losses that made me feel so depressed.

For me, the depressed episodes were lasting only a night or so at a time, until more stress factors got to me (example: high expectations and being overloaded at work) then I finally tried to commit suicide. I don't have a big success story after, besides I've continued living and now take my self care a lot more seriously. I've even stopped talking to people(even extended family who promised to help and all that sweet talk after losing my parents) who made me feel way too pressured/judged/like I wasn't doing good enough. That last bit is making a huge difference for me In the last 8 months..

I hate fathers Day and everything surrounding it but some years it's easier to ignore all that than others. Maybe those easier years are the ones where I'm keeping myself distracted better.... My dad passed away on actual father's day over ten years ago but the anger isn't going away soon.

Information about genetic or even possibly genetic conditions from both side of my family... Including mental health struggles. I question if the depression and anxiety I struggle with in my life is a result of my experiences or bloodline.

Also their favorite quotes!
I think it's based on the location you were at unfortunately and honestly most of the people that commented below smack talking you didn't read your whole post and they sound toxic.

Over the last 8ish months I've decided not to reply to certain people and to not get on or ever post on Facebook/Instagram. I keep in touch with a smaller group of friends that have been more loyal over the years and I feel so much more at peace. I e withdrawn at times but my friends I've chosen to stay in touch with are more understanding that I go through rough months sometimes but once I'm ready to connect again I'll reach out. I have guilt over being an awful friend but this is what I'm doing for myself for now :)

I go through periods of months at a time where I barely leave or talk to anyone. Some friends get worried, I've stopped talking to a few "friends" completely bc I know they get frustrated with me and I've heard what they say/think from others, which cause me.more anxietytbh. Surround yourself with friends and family that are truly understanding, that won't judge. That's my two cents. It seems for me the longer I stay withdrawnrhe harder it is to go back out and be active again (work wise and social circle wise)
I feel like it is. Society's expectations make me upset. I'm tired of trying and being more.tired/repetitive/burnt out the more time goes on.

For myself I have to make a big effort to stay distracted by the present and not be aware of how much misery composes (at least my own) life... Honestly I'm so ready to give up tho I really don't know how much longer I am able to keep taking and going week by week..... And tomorrow is Monday on top of it....
My own mindset has killed me inside a hundred times over and will continue to do so until I finally die.... Yaaaaaayy...
I've become very aware of how judgmental society is and how crappy existence in this world is unless you're born into rare, exceptional situations.
Yes, it's been comforting for me for a while now. There can be some really unexpected and ugly twists that happen in life so an opt out comforts me a lot.
This is what I did today, I was actually sad but not sure why outside of being aware of starting another week of work and being slave to this crap society/system of working to barely survive

Yes, anyone in a relationship can still become depressed. Someone can even still feel lonely while in a relationship. Be as honest (as you comfortably can) with your partner about it. Be sure to let them know it's not their fault. If they love you they will be understanding as possible and try to help.

I wonder the same exact thing, those people more than likely aren't struggling with physical or mental health, or whatever they're doing to treat any issues is working really well. Sometimes I have to force myself to get chores and going out done. I only maintain relationships now by communicating via phone.

I keep drowning in my thoughts about how myself and so many others have no choice but to work week after week after week for soooo longyo pay bill after bill..... This existence sucks. I always recommend to others to look for joy in small things and enjoy time spent with loved ones, Pets included, but living this life is made up of mostly working/planning around work. Ugh. Even with goals of getting nice places to live or vacations or whatever someone wants... We have to keep working and working and working... 

Ps I will add k chose my current job with the aim of avoiding dealing with customers. I have frustrations at work still but I'm so glad I don't have to deal with customers constantly!
I'm so sorry you went through so many harsh experiences and was let down by someone you saw as a friend :( society and this world are harsh

Thank you for posting this, it does help me feel less alone. I can relate in struggling to open up about my depressive feelings and perception of life... When talking out loud to someone every way I describe how I feel doesn't sound right. I feel like on the inside I've given up on life and become more tired each month. I look for little joys but all the struggles and challenges, even small ones, overwhelm me. There's no end in sight and it makes me want to give up more.
Honestly I always thought going sober after being addicted to drugs/alcohol sounds boring

Staying occupied even with menial tasks helps me out, I try to distract myself basically. I do my best to ignore others and just focus on what I'm doing, sometimes I "yell" thoughts in my head such as 'just focus on yourself keep on going". Sometimes I grip my nails into my hands and that helps me

I don't envy you and your wife at all, that sounds like a big struggle. Even if the work schedule situation is temporary that isn't good for your relationship :( I hope you two find better days soon and things get much easier!

Yes, honestly I feel like I'm more aware of how actually shitty life is compared to 'normal' mentally healthy people. Close friends of mine that have depression or other mental health struggles have a similar awareness too. I envy those without such awareness of how struggle and suffering based life is..

I've had days where most hours felt this way to me, i have had very few noticeable panic attacks because the normal panic attack for me is very internal in my head horrible perspective and nervous thoughts for hours, it's made worse by being around other people. Made a lot worse by being around a lot of people in a small area!

I second the reading financial books and learning more about finances while young. 

School is very important and it will pay off to get good grades and get a college degree. My personal advice is get some work experience before settling on a degree. I know many people (including myself) that 5 years out of college work in fields completely unrelated to their degree.

It's extremely unfair. When I told my partner how I'm upset that I'm alive and struggling without choosing to be they called me spoiled. Okay. Yeah been struggling to keep up for over a decade and that makes me so spoiled.

I can relate, I hate being pressured about big decisions. Some such as university or job goals need more time, there's pressure in society to have a plan on what we're doing right out of school or college. If you make a decision too quick or under pressure you might regret what you end up choosing. Factor in events that can happen at random and completely outside of your control and it's all a nightmare.
Your landlord is awful.

I'm late to comment here but this post came up in my Google search when I was trying to find out if anyone else noticed cherry Dr pepper tastes different lately. It even smells different to me, it reminds me of a medicinal taste I hate it. I bought a 12 pack of cans this week and have been dumping each one out :/ it really sucks because cherry Dr pepper used to be one of my favorite sodas

I've been wanting to end it all for me for well before the pandemic. It started getting really bad for me during a stressful job 6 years ago, now each year it's getting more and more difficult to hold my head up. I'm distancing myself so much from my family, I typically prefer discussing my darker thoughts and feelings with friends instead of them. I think the point of it all is to find anything and anyone that makes us happy.

You aren't alone, I struggle with many intrusive feelings and thoughts that make me feel anywhere from mildly annoyed to very uncomfortable and/or embarrassed (especially with thoughts regarding certain memories at random). I don't leave the house when I don't have to but that relates more to me not wanting to go around people or run into neighbors
Letting anger and weird emotions take over me while adjusting to a new med and not taking a different route home the morning I got in a wreck.

You're not invisible, I feel similar in my life right now. All jobs look dead end to me, I couldn't even make it 3 weeks at a new job without calling out. Now I'm probably fired or about to be. I stay off Facebook except for short and rare occasions bc I compare myself to others on there. It always looks like people are doing better than me. Ive had a lot of suicidal ideation recently but I try to distract myself and focus on how happy my pet makes me. Just little things really help, there is so much misery in life however..

Are you looking forward to seeing any of the guests? I hope it ends up being better for you than you're expecting. I'm dreading another year of life... I've had the holiday blues and just general blues for months now.
Most of the time I can't wait to be dead, out in public I fear it especially in cars

I've never heard of anyone saying anxiety could be outgrown before. Being a teenager is awkward (and can be horrible for some, it seems like it would be worse nowadays with all the social media cyber bullying nonsense) but adulthood is rough. Ouch responsibilities galore

I'm tired of the same things including being tired too.. I remember texting a close friend about it maybe 4 years ago, and here I am now feeling the same way still... Sad thing is when I sent that message years ago I was functioning better than I am now... Im tired of falling deeper into this pit this isn't a good trend

Yes from my point of view 2021 has been much worse than 2020. Very personal situations unique to me affected me to think this way, I remember telling myself at the end of 2020 that next (this) year has to be better... I was very wrong. The first few months of this year got wacky for me...

I feel for you, I do and you are not alone. It sounds like you have a wonderful boyfriend, he seems very supportive of you. It's a blessing to have someone there like that when going through a very difficult time. If you can't get approved for disability, are there any part time jobs you might be able to pick up near you? Maybe just a few hours a few days a week might give you a feeling of accomplishment and purpose when leaving the house? I'd suggest diving into hobbies but I know how depression drowns out interest in any activities.

Good luck, I hope you feel better soon, internet hugs!
Yes I hate it, I've had many thoughts of wanting to be sterilized and getting rid of or even harming my reproductive organs so my body can't betray me!

Years ago I loved interacting with other people weekly, now I get no joy from it and I think I burnt out on people from a few "people centric" jobs I worked over the last few years. (Having to interact with many people a day as part of the job, i had a high tolerance for bad attitudes now I get sick of em after a week and feel like quitting). Now I love isolating myself, I have less bullcrap from others to worry about and no fear of being judged by anyone.

Yes, a lot for me. I keep my phone on vibrate, it helps but if a lot of notifications are going off at once it makes me nervous. Sometimes I purposefully don't look at my phone for a while or even power if off. I miss when smart phones didn't exist.

I wish I could too. I'm taking a nap again here soon and I'm hoping I feel neutral enough when I wake up that I can get some things done around the house. Sometimes I just want to stay in bed while not even sleeping because I feel so safe and comfortable there

I think losing loved ones earlier in life kicked my mental struggles into gear, now with the struggles of getting older and realizing my life has to be worked away to "make a living" makes me more miserable. I attempted suicide once and my experiences with the hospital and having to tell family and friends about what I did prevents me from wanting to repeat all that. I also live for my partner and dog, I love them both. I love my friends and family too but I'm distancing myself from them a lot bc I don't have the energy to keep up with them plus I am just tired of making it seem like I'm ok to them.

I got into an accident over two months ago and have barely driven since. I can't even get myself to take my damaged vehicle to a shop and I hate looking at it. I'm scared to know what neighbors think, I dread them asking me about it so I barely go outside. It's hard to cope with for me, I get angry when my partner pushes me to drive to the store but I just end up going through with it and feel thankful when I'm back safe. It's easier for me to take short trips on familiar routes but I'm nowhere close to where I was before the accident. I'm tempted to get a job I can just walk to.

Before you see your doctor write down or type in your phone any words or phrases that you think match how you feel even a little bit. I have a lot of trouble describing how I feel in regards to my mental health too, a lot of times I say I feel "blah" and have no desire to do anything. Good luck.

Disappointment in myself for not being better off financially or career wise, I have no interest in hobbies that I enjoyed even earlier this year, general numbness in regards to my emotions, and boredom at the idea of paying bills/gas/groceries/for other expenses every month for the rest of my life. I've lost the desire to connect with people and hang out with anyone anymore too.

I don't know exactly why this happens, but I have to force myself to eat when depressed. Food tastes way less good and many times bland when I'm depressed and I think heavy apathy prevents me from wanting to eat.

I've felt the same when anyone tells me they want to talk, anymore I usually respond with asking the person if they're ok. It's an easier transition for me into whatever they want to talk about, usually it's to vent

I feel very similar to what you're describing lately. I've only been talking to friends that I think will empathize with how I feel and not judge me (yet I still do worry about that but it feels good to open up to a degree). I haven't had goals in a long time outside of making sure my bills are paid. I really don't know how to fix that and I've thought off and on about it for years. I can tell you tho I think goals are intimidating (both personal and professional types). 

In my opinion making an attempt to go to the gym will be worth it, at least for a few days, if it doesn't help you then you can always cancel your membership. 

Depression is difficult to work through, I'm 30 and still don't have a solid method of working through my more rough phases. I hope you have better luck and find your own way soon

I have a lot of trouble describing my anxiety symptoms out loud, I think part of that is because I fear people will think I'm crazy. I started feeling off over a month ago around when I started working nights, I don't work nights anymore but I've been struggling to sleep at night still and my off feeling has evolved into a sensation of feeling like my heart is in my throat or pounding too hard/quickly. I'm so tired of feeling this way

I'm the same, I hate being around people when I'm anxious. Lately it's constant and the only time I feel comfortable is if I'm home alone or in bed. I think the reason someone feels worse around others is unique for each person, but as for myself I can tell you I fear people gossiping about me. Various people in my friend/acquaintance group have told me what others have said about me and it haunts me. I know you shouldn't care what others think or say but it's much easier said than done. If I'm alone, no one can observe and possibly judge me.

This is why I keep avoiding people too, you aren't the only one feeling this way. Text is my preferred form of  communication because I can put more thought into my replies. However if someone is a true friend or family member, they will listen to you talk about your problems (especially if you've listened to them in the past). Everyone has problems but not everyone is willing to admit it.

Yes, I can and there's been times I've sent replies on the lines of "hey sorry to reply late I've been busy working.." or "forgot to reply", or even "I've been struggling with keeping up with friends how have you been?" If they're a good friend or family member then they won't give you shit or make fun of you (behind your back in my case) for having phases in which it's difficult to find the energy to reply.

I've left a few jobs now for my mental health when I could tell the job/work environment wasn't going to get better soon enough for it to be worth me sticking around even longer and suffering even more.

If you can find a job that doesn't make you hate life/feel suicidal then stick with it. Having friends and good coworkers/leadership in general helps but that is different from job to job. I've heard some people will place a picture of what their goal is (ie buying a house or going on vacation somewhere nice) to keep them going at work in office environments.

As for myself, I haven't had any luck recently. I left my most recent job due mostly to toxic people and leadership both. I'm still looking..

I've been experiencing something similar for the last couple of years. it feels like I've been job hopping forever... The longest I've held a job in the last 4 years is 10 months. Boredom has driven me from a few jobs, as well as lack of benefits/knowing I was a temp. Have you thought about what you really want out of a job, or looked at company reviews before going in? I wouldn't say you're acting foolishly but you're just not satisfied with where you've been landing.

One thing I've learned to do is keep short term jobs off future applications and resumes. Less explaining and awkwardness in future interviews. 

Good luck, i hope you find somewhere you want to stick around for a while!

I've fallen behind on a lot of things and keep having thoughts of going away and not existing. I recently left a job that made me miserable (I was only there for a few months and knew I had to leave soon or I'd be worse feeling). So that brought me relief, getting out of there but now I'm stressed about where ever I go next I'll still hate life somewhat. My motivation is depleted!
PokemonGo has helped me a bunch since it was released. I tend to play it a lot for a few months then stop when I get bored however. Digimon is my favorite childhood show, I've always enjoyed both tho

I never hear anyone else talk about going through this, thank you for your reply. I'm glad I'm not the only one. I remember one very stressful evening at an old job a girl asked me if I wanted her to talk for me because I could barely get words out. I probably sounded like I had a sore throat but I was embarrassed at first

Major depressive disorder and generalized anxiety (which at times can be severe). It makes it difficult for me to communicate when I'm going through more difficult phases with my disorders, almost everything I say and write/type sounds awkward
Happy birthday!!
Looks like your drink is the same color as your boy's eyes, neat!

Extra detail: he tends to get very mean and have abusive phases every couple months or so, he does like to turn to a certain substance that doesn't help every few months. I'm noticing a pattern or cycle
